accessibilityExpert.description: Answer accessibility, a11y, and WCAG questions using BrowserStack's accessibility knowledge base.

authConfigId.description: Optional auth config ID for authenticated scans

advancedRules.description: Enable advanced accessibility rules in the scan settings

createAccessibilityAuthConfig.description: Create an authentication configuration for accessibility scans. Supports both form-based and basic authentication.

type.description: Authentication type: 'form' for form-based auth, 'basic' for HTTP basic auth

username.description: Site username; omit to have it requested from the user.

password.description: Site password; omit to have it requested from the user.

fetchAccessibilityIssues.description: Fetch accessibility issues from a completed scan with pagination support. Use cursor parameter to get subsequent pages of results. scanRunId.description: The scan run ID from a completed accessibility scan

setupBrowserStackAutomateTests.description: Set up and run automated web-based tests on BrowserStack using the BrowserStack SDK. Use this tool for functional or integration test setup on BrowserStack only. For any visual testing or Percy integration, use the dedicated Percy setup tool. Example prompts: run this test on browserstack; set up this project for browserstack.

projectName.description: A single name for your project to organize all your tests.

devices.description: Device objects array. Use the object format directly - no transformation needed. Add only when user explicitly requests devices. Examples: [{ platform: 'windows', osVersion: '11', browser: 'chrome', browserVersion: 'latest' }] or [{ platform: 'android', deviceName: 'Samsung Galaxy S24', osVersion: '14', browser: 'chrome' }].

deviceName.description: Device name for mobile platforms, e.g. 'iPhone 15', 'Samsung Galaxy S24'

browserVersion.description: Browser version for desktop platforms only (windows, macos), e.g. '132', 'latest', 'oldest'. Not used for mobile devices (android, ios).

percyVisualTestIntegrationAgent.description: Integrate Percy visual testing into new projects and demonstrate visual change detection through a step-by-step simulation. This tool handles initial Percy integration, setup, and creates a working demonstration for new users. Primary tool for prompts like: "Integrate percy for this project", "Integrate percy in this project {project_name}"

projectName.description: A unique name for your Percy project.

integrationType.description: Specify the Percy integration type: web (Percy Web) or automate (Percy Automate). If not provided, always prompt the user with: 'Please specify the Percy integration type.' Do not proceed without an explicit selection. Never use a default.

folderPaths.description: An array of absolute folder paths containing UI test files. If not provided, analyze codebase for UI test folders by scanning for test patterns which contain UI test cases as per framework. Return empty array if none found.

filePaths.description: An array of absolute file paths to specific UI test files. Use this when you want to target specific test files rather than entire folders. If not provided, will use folderPaths instead.

expandPercyVisualTesting.description: Set up or expand Percy visual testing configuration with comprehensive coverage for existing projects that might have Percy integrated. This supports both Percy Web Standalone and Percy Automate. Example prompts: Expand percy coverage for this project {project_name}

projectName.description: A unique name for your Percy project.

integrationType.description: Specify the Percy integration type: web (Percy Web) or automate (Percy Automate). If not provided, always prompt the user with: 'Please specify the Percy integration type.' Do not proceed without an explicit selection. Never use a default.

folderPaths.description: An array of absolute folder paths containing UI test files. If not provided, analyze codebase for UI test folders by scanning for test patterns which contain UI test cases as per framework. Return empty array if none found.

filePaths.description: An array of absolute file paths to specific UI test files. Use this when you want to target specific test files rather than entire folders. If not provided, will use folderPaths instead.

addPercySnapshotCommands.description: Adds Percy snapshot commands to the specified test files.

index.description: Index of the test file to update

listTestFiles.description: Lists all test files for a given set of directories.

runPercyScan.description: Run a Percy visual test scan. Example prompts : Run this Percy build/scan. Never run percy scan/build without this tool

projectName.description: The name of the project to run Percy on.

percyRunCommand.description: The test command to run with Percy. Optional — the LLM should try to infer it first from project context.

integrationType.description: Specifies whether to integrate with Percy Web or Percy Automate. If not explicitly provided, prompt the user to select the desired integration type.

fetchPercyChanges.description: Retrieves and summarizes all visual changes detected by Percy AI between the latest and previous builds, helping quickly review what has changed in your project.

project_name.description: The name of the BrowserStack project. If not found, ask user directly.

managePercyBuildApproval.description: Approve or reject a Percy build

buildId.description: The ID of the Percy build to approve or reject.

action.description: The action to perform on the Percy build.

runAppLiveSession.description: Use this tool when user wants to manually check their app on a particular mobile device using BrowserStack's cloud infrastructure. Can be used to debug crashes, slow performance, etc.

desiredPhone.description: The full name of the device to run the app on. Example: 'iPhone 12 Pro' or 'Samsung Galaxy S20' or 'Google Pixel 6'. Always ask the user for the device they want to use, do not assume it.

desiredPlatformVersion.description: Specifies the platform version to run the app on. For example, use '12.0' for Android or '16.0' for iOS. If the user says 'latest', 'newest', or similar, normalize it to 'latest'. Likewise, convert terms like 'earliest' or 'oldest' to 'oldest'.

desiredPlatform.description: Which platform to run on, examples: 'android', 'ios'. Set this based on the app path provided.

appPath.description: The path to the .ipa or .apk file to install on the device. Always ask the user for the app path, do not assume it. Must be located inside the directory set in MCP_UPLOAD_BASE_DIR.

runBrowserLiveSession.description: Launch a BrowserStack Live session (desktop or mobile).

desiredOS.description: Desktop OS ('Windows' or 'OS X') or mobile OS ('android','ios','winphone')

desiredOSVersion.description: The OS version must be specified as a version number (e.g., '10', '14.0') or as a keyword such as 'latest' or 'oldest'. Normalize variations like 'newest' or 'most recent' to 'latest', and terms like 'earliest' or 'first' to 'oldest'. For macOS, version names (e.g., 'Sequoia') must be used instead of numeric versions.

desiredBrowser.description: Browser for desktop (Chrome, IE, Firefox, Safari, Edge)

desiredBrowserVersion.description: Browser version for desktop (e.g. '133.2', 'latest'). If the user says 'latest', 'newest', or similar, normalize it to 'latest'. Likewise, convert terms like 'earliest' or 'oldest' to 'oldest'.

createProjectOrFolder.description: Create a project and/or folder in BrowserStack Test Management. Creating a project needs no identifier. Creating a folder inside an EXISTING project needs that project's identifier (PR-*); no tool here lists projects, so use the capability functions to look it up.

project_name.description: Name of the project to create.

project_identifier.description: Existing project identifier to use for folder creation.

folder_name.description: Name of the folder to create.

parent_id.description: Parent folder ID; if omitted, folder is created at root.

createTestCase.description: Use this tool to create a test case in BrowserStack Test Management. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, use the capability functions to list the Test Management projects, then retry this tool with the identifier they return.

project_identifier.description: The ID of the BrowserStack project where the test case should be created. If no project identifier is provided, ask the user if they would like to create a new project using the createProjectOrFolder tool.

folder_id.description: The ID of the folder within the project where the test case should be created. If not provided, ask the user if they would like to create a new folder using the createProjectOrFolder tool.

description.description: Brief description of the test case.

owner.description: Email of the test case owner.

step.description: Action to perform in this step.

test_case_steps.description: List of steps and expected results.

issues.description: List of the linked Jira, Asana or Azure issues ID's. This should be strictly in array format not the string of json.

name.description: Issue tracker name,  For example, use jira for Jira, azure for Azure DevOps, or asana for Asana.

host.description: Base URL of the issue tracker.

tags.description: Tags to attach to the test case. This should be strictly in array format not the string of json

custom_fields.description: Map of custom field NAME to value; use an array for multi-select fields.

automation_status.description: Automation status of the test case. Common values include 'not_automated', 'automated', 'automation_not_required'.

priority.description: Priority of the test case. Accepts either display name (e.g. 'Critical', 'High', 'Medium', 'Low') or internal name (e.g. 'medium'). If omitted, the project default (usually 'Medium') is applied. Valid values are per-project and discoverable via the form-fields endpoint.

case_type.description: Test case type display or internal name (per-project). Omit for project default.

template.description: System template slug only: 'test_case_steps' or 'test_case_bdd'. For a custom template, use template_id instead.

template_id.description: Numeric ID of a custom template (from listTestCaseTemplates); applies that template. Overrides 'template'.

updateTestCase.description: Update an existing test case in BrowserStack Test Management. Any subset of the following fields may be changed: name, description, preconditions, test_case_steps, owner, priority, case_type, automation_status, status, tags, issues, custom_fields. Only the supplied fields are modified. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, use the capability functions to list the Test Management projects, then retry this tool with the identifier they return.

project_identifier.description: The ID of the BrowserStack project containing the test case to update.

test_case_identifier.description: The ID of the test case to update. This can be found using the listTestCases tool.

name.description: Updated name of the test case.

description.description: Updated brief description of the test case.

preconditions.description: Updated preconditions for the test case.

test_case_steps.description: Updated list of test case steps with expected results.

step.description: The action to perform in this step.

result.description: The expected result of this step.

owner.description: Email of the test case owner.

priority.description: Updated priority. Accepts either display name (e.g. 'Medium', 'Critical', 'High', 'Low') or internal name (e.g. 'medium'). Valid values are per-project and discoverable via the form-fields endpoint.

case_type.description: Updated test case type. Accepts either display name (e.g. 'Functional', 'Regression', 'Smoke & Sanity') or internal name (e.g. 'functional', 'smoke_sanity'). Valid values are per-project.

automation_status.description: Updated automation status. Use internal name such as 'not_automated', 'automated', 'automation_not_required', 'cannot_be_automated', or 'obsolete'.

status.description: Updated review status of the test case (e.g. 'active', 'draft', 'in_review', 'outdated', 'rejected').

tags.description: Replacement list of tags for the test case.

issues.description: Replacement list of linked Jira/Asana/Azure issue IDs for the test case.

custom_fields.description: Map of custom field NAME to value; use an array for multi-select fields.

listTestCases.description: List test cases in a project, optionally scoped to a specific folder. Omit folder_id to list all test cases in the project; provide folder_id (discoverable via listFolders) to list only that folder's cases. Supports filters: case_type, priority, pagination. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, use the capability functions to list the Test Management projects, then retry this tool with the identifier they return.

project_identifier.description: Identifier of the project to fetch test cases from. This id starts with a PR- and is followed by a number.

folder_id.description: Optional. If provided, only return test cases in this folder. If omitted, returns all test cases in the project. Folder ids can be discovered via listFolders.

case_type.description: Comma-separated list of case types (e.g. functional,regression).

listFolders.description: List folders in a BrowserStack Test Management project, returning each folder's id and name (plus case counts and sub-folder counts). Pass parent_id to list sub-folders under a specific folder instead of top-level folders. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, use the capability functions to list the Test Management projects, then retry this tool with the identifier they return.

project_identifier.description: Identifier of the project to fetch folders from (starts with PR- followed by a number).

parent_id.description: If provided, list sub-folders under this parent folder id. If omitted, lists top-level folders.

listTestCaseTemplates.description: List test-case templates with their numeric template_id. Use the id with createTestCase to apply a custom template (the 'template' slug only selects system templates).

name.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on template name.

createTestRun.description: Create a test run in BrowserStack Test Management. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, use the capability functions to list the Test Management projects, then retry this tool with the identifier they return.

project_identifier.description: Identifier of the project in which to create the test run.

description.description: Brief information about the test run

run_state.description: State of the test run. One of new_run, in_progress, under_review, rejected, done, closed

listTestRuns.description: List test runs in a project with optional filters (date ranges, assignee, state, etc.) Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, use the capability functions to list the Test Management projects, then retry this tool with the identifier they return.

project_identifier.description: Identifier of the project to fetch test runs from (usually starts with PR-).

run_state.description: Return all test runs with this state (comma-separated)

updateTestRun.description: Update a test run's metadata and/or add test cases to it. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, use the capability functions to list the Test Management projects, then retry this tool with the identifier they return.

name.description: New name of the test run

run_state.description: Updated state of the test run

add_test_cases.description: Test cases to add to the run

preserve_existing_results.description: Keep existing results when adding cases (default true)

addTestResult.description: Add a test result to a specific test run via BrowserStack Test Management API. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, use the capability functions to list the Test Management projects, then retry this tool with the identifier they return.

test_run_id.description: Identifier of the test run (e.g., TR-678)

status.description: Status of the test result, e.g., 'passed', 'failed'.

test_case_id.description: Identifier of the test case, e.g., 'TC-13'.

uploadProductRequirementFile.description: Upload files (e.g., PDRs, PDFs) to BrowserStack Test Management and retrieve a file mapping ID. This is utilized for generating test cases from files and is part of the Test Case Generator AI Agent in BrowserStack. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, use the capability functions to list the Test Management projects, then retry this tool with the identifier they return.

project_identifier.description: ID of the project where the file should be uploaded. Do not assume it, always ask user for it.

file_path.description: Full path to the file that should be uploaded. Must be inside the directory configured via the MCP_UPLOAD_BASE_DIR environment variable.

createTestCasesFromFile.description: Generate test cases from a file in BrowserStack Test Management using the Test Case Generator AI Agent.

projectReferenceId.description: The BrowserStack project reference ID is a unique identifier found in the project URL within the BrowserStack Test Management Platform. This ID is also returned by the Upload Document tool.

createLCASteps.description: Generate Low Code Automation (LCA) steps for a test case in BrowserStack Test Management using the Low Code Automation Agent. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, use the capability functions to list the Test Management projects, then retry this tool with the identifier they return.

requires_authentication.description: Set true if the test case requires login.

credentials.description: Login credentials; omit to have them requested from the user.

test_case_steps.description: Array of test case steps with expected results

wait_for_completion.description: Whether to wait for LCA build completion (default: true)

listTestPlans.description: List test plans in a BrowserStack Test Management project. Returns each plan's identifier (TP-*), name, status, description, dates, and active/closed test-run counts. Supports pagination. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, use the capability functions to list the Test Management projects, then retry this tool with the identifier they return. Creating a test plan or sub-plan, and linking or unlinking test runs on one, are not available as tools here: use the capability functions, which reach Test Management's own API for these operations. They ask you to confirm before changing anything.

project_identifier.description: Identifier of the project to fetch test plans from (starts with PR- followed by a number).

getTestPlan.description: Fetch a test plan by identifier (TP-*) from BrowserStack Test Management. Returns plan metadata, the full list of linked test runs, total test-case count across runs, and a status summary — suitable for generating test documentation or QA status reports. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, use the capability functions to list the Test Management projects, then retry this tool with the identifier they return. Requires a test plan identifier (TP-*). Call listTestPlans first if you do not have it. Creating a test plan or sub-plan, and linking or unlinking test runs on one, are not available as tools here: use the capability functions, which reach Test Management's own API for these operations. They ask you to confirm before changing anything.

project_identifier.description: Identifier of the project (starts with PR- followed by a number).

test_plan_identifier.description: Identifier of the test plan (starts with TP- followed by a number).

listSubTestPlans.description: List sub-test-plans under a parent test plan (TP-*) in a Test Management project. Supports pagination. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, use the capability functions to list the Test Management projects, then retry this tool with the identifier they return. Requires a test plan identifier (TP-*). Call listTestPlans first if you do not have it. Creating a test plan or sub-plan, and linking or unlinking test runs on one, are not available as tools here: use the capability functions, which reach Test Management's own API for these operations. They ask you to confirm before changing anything.

getSubTestPlan.description: Fetch a sub-test-plan (STP-*) under a parent plan (TP-*). Returns metadata and linked test runs. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, use the capability functions to list the Test Management projects, then retry this tool with the identifier they return. Requires a test plan identifier (TP-*). Call listTestPlans first if you do not have it. Creating a test plan or sub-plan, and linking or unlinking test runs on one, are not available as tools here: use the capability functions, which reach Test Management's own API for these operations. They ask you to confirm before changing anything.

takeAppScreenshot.description: Use this tool to take a screenshot of an app running on a BrowserStack device. This is useful for visual testing and debugging.

desiredPhone.description: The full name of the device to run the app on. Example: 'iPhone 12 Pro' or 'Samsung Galaxy S20'. Always ask the user for the device they want to use.

desiredPlatformVersion.description: The platform version to run the app on. Use 'latest' or 'oldest' for dynamic resolution.

appPath.description: The path to the .apk or .ipa file. Required for app installation. Must be located inside the directory set in MCP_UPLOAD_BASE_DIR.

runAppTestsOnBrowserStack.description: Execute pre-built native mobile test suites (Espresso for Android, XCUITest for iOS) by direct upload to BrowserStack. ONLY for compiled .apk/.ipa test files. This is NOT for SDK integration or Appium tests. For Appium-based testing with SDK setup, use 'setupBrowserStackAppAutomateTests' instead.

appPath.description:
Path to your application file:
If in development IDE directory:
• For Android: 'gradle assembleDebug'
• For iOS:
  xcodebuild clean -scheme YOUR_SCHEME && \
  xcodebuild archive -scheme YOUR_SCHEME -configuration Release -archivePath build/app.xcarchive && \
  xcodebuild -exportArchive -archivePath build/app.xcarchive -exportPath build/ipa -exportOptionsPlist exportOptions.plist

If in other directory, provide existing app path.
The resolved file must be located inside the directory set in MCP_UPLOAD_BASE_DIR.

testSuitePath.description:
Path to your test suite file:
If in development IDE directory:
• For Android: 'gradle assembleAndroidTest'
• For iOS:
  xcodebuild test-without-building -scheme YOUR_SCHEME -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' && \
  cd ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/*/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/ && \
  zip -r Tests.zip *.xctestrun *-Runner.app

If in other directory, provide existing test file path.
The resolved file must be located inside the directory set in MCP_UPLOAD_BASE_DIR.

getFailureLogs.description: Fetch logs, or the session video URL, for an Automate/App Automate session. Requires a session id. listSessions lists them for a build; if you do not have the build either, getBuildId or listBuildId resolves one from a project and build name.

sessionType.description: Type of BrowserStack session. Must be explicitly provided by the user.

sessionId.description: The BrowserStack session ID. Must be explicitly provided by the user.

buildId.description: App Automate build ID. Optional — resolved from the session if omitted.

limit.description: Max sessions to return. Defaults to 10.

offset.description: Pagination offset for the REST session list.

status.description: Optional session status filter (e.g. done, running, error). Applied client-side.

fetchSelfHealedSelectors.description: Fetch BrowserStack self-healed selectors plus the test source code for the run. Provide exactly one of `sessionId` (single Automate / App-Automate session) or `buildUuid` (full self-healing report for a build). Pass the returned locator pairs to `prepareSelfHealingPlan` to plan edits. Requires a session id. listSessions lists them for a build; if you do not have the build either, getBuildId or listBuildId resolves one from a project and build name.

sessionId.description: Session ID. Mutually exclusive with buildUuid.

sessionType.description: Used with sessionId. Defaults to automate.

buildUuid.description: Build UUID. Fetches the build's self-healing report.

prepareSelfHealingPlan.description: Build a self-healing edit plan that bundles locator pairs with test source code for the calling LLM to apply with its own editing tools. This tool does NOT modify files — it returns structured context so the LLM can edit only the relevant call sites (avoids blind find/replace across shared ids/classes). `sessions` accepts the canonical shape `[{sessionId, locators: [{original, healed, thought?}]}]`, a single session object, an envelope `{sessions: [...]}`, the raw report `{healing_logs: [...]}` (with `healed_selectors` aliasing `locators`), and snake_case keys (`session_id`, `original_locator`, `healed_locator`, `healing_thought`). Requires a session id. listSessions lists them for a build; if you do not have the build either, getBuildId or listBuildId resolves one from a project and build name.

sessions.description: Sessions to plan edits for. See tool description for accepted shapes.

locators.description: Healed locator pairs for this session.

fetchBuildInsights.description: Fetch build details and quality gate results. Includes hashed_id and session_type for listSessions.

buildId.description: The build UUID of the BrowserStack build

fetchRCA.description: Fetch AI Root Cause Analysis for the current user's failed BrowserStack Automate/App-Automate tests. Suggests fixes only; never auto-apply, require explicit user approval. Requires test ids. Call listTestIds first if you do not have it.

browserStackBuildName.description: BrowserStack build name from the test run config (e.g. browserstack.yml). Exact match; no default.

listBuildId.description: Get the latest build ID for a project and build name, across all users (no user filter).

browserStackProjectName.description: BrowserStack project name from the test run config (e.g. browserstack.yml). Exact match; no default.

browserStackBuildName.description: BrowserStack build name from the test run config (e.g. browserstack.yml). Exact match; no default.

listTestIds.description: List all tests of a BrowserStack build (each with its status and session id); optional status filter. Requires a BrowserStack build id. Call getBuildId or listBuildId first if you do not have it.

status.description: Filter tests by status. If not provided, all tests are returned. Example for RCA usecase always use failed status

includeFailureDetail.description: Add per-test failure signature for clustering. Default false.

askBrowserStackAI.description: (Alpha, limited availability. Enabled per account and per product; if it is not enabled the call returns an entitlement error, nothing runs, and you should complete the task with the individual tools instead. To request access, the user should contact their BrowserStack account owner.) Use this when no other BrowserStack tool here fits the task, or when the ones you tried did not get you there. Prefer a specific tool whenever one fits: it is faster and more predictable than handing the job to an agent. Otherwise, describe what you want in plain language and BrowserStack's agent decides which calls to make, then returns its answer plus the steps it took. Anything that would change data pauses and asks you to confirm it first; deletes are refused outright. Put that confirmation to the user and answer with what THEY say — never decide on their behalf. If it cannot be put to anyone, the run is read-only and everything it wanted to change comes back in `needs_approval` instead. One task per call.

product.description: Which product to work in: tm (Test Management), tra (Test Reporting & Analytics).

query.description: What you want, in plain language. One thing per call.

decision.description: The user's answer. Never assume allow — ask them.

listProducts.description: List the BrowserStack products this surface can reach: what each one does, the entities it models, and a line saying what each entity is. START HERE — searchCapability needs a product, and this is what tells you which one. If two products could both fit the task, ask the user rather than choosing for them. ALWAYS pass the user's request, in their own words, as `query`: the answer then says outright whether the products clash over the words in it. WHEN IT REPORTS A CLASH — two products claiming the same word for different things — ASK THE USER WHICH PRODUCT THEY MEAN AND WAIT FOR THEIR ANSWER BEFORE SEARCHING OR INVOKING ANYTHING. The response carries the question to put to them and what the shared word means in each product. Choosing for them, or searching each product in turn and merging the results, is the failure this call exists to prevent.

query.description: The user's request, in their own words. With it the response carries a `routing` block saying whether the products share the vocabulary this request uses — and, when they do, the question to put to the user before searching either product.

describeEntity.description: Describe one entity: what it is, what identifies it, what it relates to, and the vocabulary the product uses for it. Read this before filtering or writing, because ids and field values usually have to be resolved first.

product.description: Which product the entity belongs to: loadtesting, tm, tra.

entity.description: Entity name, as listProducts returns it.

searchCapability.description: Find endpoints this surface can call, by plain language, within ONE product. CALL listProducts FIRST, passing the user's request as its `query`: it names the products, says whether they clash over the words in that request, and gives you the question to ask when they do. You need it anyway — `product` here takes a name exactly as listProducts spells it. Where two products use the same word for different things, ask the USER and wait for an answer rather than picking. Search matches the product's OWN words, not synonyms. When your words are not the product's, the response says so: `weak_match: true` with a `suggested_vocabulary` map of the product's entities and their aliases. Results are still returned, but treat them as unconfirmed — pick the closest entity from that map and search again using its vocabulary, or call describeEntity on it for the fuller picture. That one extra round trip is far cheaper than invoking the wrong capability. Narrowing further with `entity` sharpens results. THIS IS A SHORTLIST, NOT A CONTRACT. Each result carries only what you need to CHOOSE: `name` (the handle), `product`, `mode` (whether it writes), `intent` and `guidance` (what it does and what goes wrong), and `method`/`path` for products that publish no name yet. It does NOT carry parameters or response shapes. Once you have picked one, call describeCapability for its full contract, then invokeCapability. Fetching the contract only for the one you chose is the difference between ~1k and ~8.6k tokens a search. Results are ranked and capped. TO SEE EVERYTHING rather than search, pass query='*' — that lists the product (honouring `entity` and `mode`) in a stable order instead of ranking it, which is what you want when the task is 'what can this product do' rather than a lookup. TO PAGE, send `offset`: every response carries `offset` and, when more matched, `next_offset` — resend the SAME query with that value. `next_offset` is absent on the last page, so walk until it stops rather than comparing counts.

query.description: What you are trying to do, in plain language. Pass '*' (or 'all') to BROWSE instead of search: every capability in the product, in a stable order, paginated — use it when you want to see the surface rather than find one thing.

entity.description: Restrict to one entity (listProducts names them).

product.description: Which product to search, named exactly as listProducts spells it. Call listProducts with the user's request to get the name — and to find out whether the products clash over it, in which case ask the user first.

routing_token.description: The `routing_token` from the last listProducts call or product_ambiguous refusal — it carries what that step concluded about the user's request, signed. Always pass the most recent one. When it reports a clash, send the user's answer in `user_words` alongside it; neither works alone.

user_words.description: The USER'S OWN words, verbatim, that settle which product this is — either the product's name or a term only one product uses ('quality gate', 'test plan'). Quote them; do not paraphrase, and do not write words the user did not say. When a query could mean either product this is what lifts the refusal, because it is checked against the index rather than taken on trust.

mode.description: Restrict to reads or writes. Omit to let the query decide.

offset.description: Skip this many results — send the `next_offset` from the previous response with the SAME query to get the next page. Omit for the first page.

describeCapability.description: The full contract for ONE capability you picked from searchCapability: its parameters grouped into path_params / query / body under the spec's own names, what it returns, and its declared response shapes fully expanded. Call this after search and before invokeCapability — search deliberately omits all of it, because it is only needed for the one capability you actually call. Identify it by `name`, exactly as search returned it; only when a result carries no `name` (some products publish none yet) pass `method` and `path` instead. Every parameter lists its type, whether it is required, its allowed values where the set is closed, and any limits the product declares — obey those before calling rather than discovering them from a rejected request.

name.description: The capability's published name, exactly as searchCapability returned it.

method.description: HTTP method — only for capabilities returned without a `name`.

path.description: Path with {placeholders} intact — only for capabilities returned without a `name`.

product.description: Which product owns it (loadtesting, tm, tra). searchCapability returns it on every result; required only when two products share a name or a path.

include_responses.description: Which declared responses to expand: 'success' (default, the 2xx shape), 'all' (adds the error shapes — several times larger, and near-identical across endpoints), or 'none'.

invokeCapability.description: Call a capability whose contract you have from describeCapability. Pass `name` exactly as given — that is the handle. Only when a result carries no `name` (some products do not publish them yet) pass `method` and `path` instead, exactly as returned. Arguments go in path_params / query / body under the spec's own names. One call makes exactly one request and returns the product's own response untouched; when `completed` is false there is another page, which you fetch by sending the capability's own page parameter. If the mode is 'write' you MUST ask the user first, then resend with user_permission='granted' and a change_summary; both are recorded. Capabilities whose mode is 'destructive' (deletes) are refused outright — archiving, closing and merging are ordinary writes and DO run, so read the mode and intent before confirming with the user.

name.description: The capability's published name, exactly as returned (e.g. 'create_test_run_by_integer_id'). Preferred over method/path.

method.description: HTTP method — only for capabilities returned without a `name`.

path.description: Path with {placeholders} intact — only for capabilities returned without a `name`.

body.description: Body fields, under the spec's names.

product.description: Which product owns the capability (loadtesting, tm, tra). searchCapability returns it on every result; required only when two products share a name or a path.

user_permission.description: Set to 'granted' only after the user has confirmed a write.

change_summary.description: What will change. Required for writes.
